findings.title: Invalid CSS property -webkit-order in order mixin
findings.body: The `order` mixin outputs `-webkit-order: $val;` on line 129, but no browser ever shipped an `-webkit-order` property. The 2009 WebKit flexbox spec used `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` (already emitted on line 126) and the 2012/modern spec uses the unprefixed `order` (emitted on line 130). The `-webkit-order` declaration is dead/invalid CSS and should be removed.

findings.title: Invalid CSS property -ms-align-items in align-items mixin
findings.body: The `align-items` mixin outputs `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` on line 121, but IE10/IE11 implement `align-items` as `-ms-flex-align` (already emitted on line 120). There is no `-ms-align-items` property in any CSS specification; the declaration is invalid and will be ignored by every browser. It should be removed.

findings.title: Bullet badge vertical alignment likely broken in extra-info-wrapper
findings.body: The change adds `line-height: 1.5` to `.extra-info-wrapper` and removes the `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule that previously compensated for the bullet badge's vertical positioning inside this wrapper. The bullet badge in `badges.css.scss` is an `inline-flex` element with `align-items: baseline`; with the new explicit `line-height: 1.5` on the parent, the baseline metric changes and the deleted 5px top margin will cause the bullet to sit visibly higher (or lower) relative to the surrounding text, producing a vertical misalignment regression for category bullets in the topic header.

findings.title: .small-action-desc loses left indent that compensated for the avatar
findings.body: The `.small-action-desc` padding was changed from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px;` to `padding: 0 1.5%`. While the parent is now a flex container and the floated 45px avatar no longer overlaps the text, removing the 4em left indent means the description text now starts directly against the avatar (separated only by the default 0px flex gap and the small 1.5% inner padding). The old 4em indent was visually meaningful; the new layout will look noticeably more cramped, and the 0 vertical padding combined with `align-items: center` removes all internal breathing room around the description text. This is a visual regression even if no overlap occurs.
